extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computer vision and machine learning (especially those working on tiny-object classification, medical or hyperspectral imaging)
extracted.subtask_short: tiny object classification in large images
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and designing convolutional neural network architectures and datasets for classifying very small objects embedded in much larger images (e.g., medical/histopathology, hyperspectral). Emphasis on controlled experiments across signal-to-noise ratios, dataset size, receptive field, and pooling choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) limit for generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a limit to signal-to-noise below which CNNs fail to generalize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report SNR when evaluating tiny-object classification. Expect a threshold SNR under which standard CNN architectures will not generalize; use controlled experiments across a spectrum of SNR values to identify this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset size affects SNR limit and generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: This SNR limit is affected by dataset size — more data leads to better performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger training sets can push the generalization threshold to lower SNRs. When assessing architectures, vary dataset size to quantify how performance scales with added data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of training data scales with inverse object-to-image ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of training data required for the model to generalize scales rapidly with the inverse of the object-to-image ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate object-to-image ratio (object area / image area). As objects become smaller relative to the image, expect required training data to grow quickly; plan dataset collection accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model capacity correlates with generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, higher capacity models exhibit better generalization for tiny-object classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider using higher-capacity architectures (more parameters / representational power) when target objects are tiny; evaluate capacity trade-offs (overfitting, computation) empirically on controlled benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapting receptive field to known object size
rubrics_metrics.description: When knowing the approximate object sizes, adapting receptive field is beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design network architectures (kernel sizes, strides, dilation, pooling) to produce receptive fields appropriate to expected object sizes. If object scale is known, tune receptive field to capture the object without excessive background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of global pooling operation matters at very low SNR
rubrics_metrics.description: For very small signal-to-noise ratio the choice of global pooling operation affects optimization, whereas for relatively large signal-to-noise values, all tested global pooling operations exhibit similar performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At low SNR evaluate different global pooling strategies (e.g., average, max, other aggregations) because they can affect optimization and final performance; at higher SNR pooling choice may be less critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset bias: object size and position distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Most CNNs were developed using biased datasets that contain large objects, in mostly central image positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that training/test datasets reflect the target distribution of object sizes and positions. Avoid relying on architectures or preprocessing tuned to central, large objects when the domain contains tiny, dispersed objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use controlled testbeds covering a spectrum of conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Build comprehensive testbeds (e.g., datasets derived from MNIST digits and histopathology images) to stress-test CNN architectures with a broad spectrum of signal-to-noise ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use synthetic or derived datasets to systematically vary SNR, object-to-image ratio, and dataset size to reveal architecture strengths and failure modes. Report experimental settings and variability so comparisons are meaningful.
